## Overview

Speeds up fp16 prefill in `RDNAHybridW4A16LinearKernel` on gfx1151 (Strix Halo). The Triton prefill GEMM dequantizes two 4-bit weights per instruction, and gets tiles tuned for that dequant. Supersedes draft #55711.

## Claims

- fp16 prefill latency on gfx1151: 5–18% faster on Qwen3-4B (symmetric) at every prompt length from 64 to 2048 tokens, and 17–19% faster on Qwen3-8B (asymmetric) from 512 tokens, unchanged below.
- No change for bf16, or on any GPU other than gfx1151.
- No accuracy change: the dequant arithmetic is exact, and kernel output is bit-identical to main in all 1248 configs swept.

## Validation

All measurements: gfx1151 (Radeon 8060S), torch 2.13.0+rocm10.2, Triton 3.8.0. main is c83935b300. Benchmarks ran on 23a1a2b640, which differs from this PR's head only in comments and in where `packed_dequant` is decided (same result for every dtype, zero-point and M). GSM8K and tests ran on the head.

**End-to-end prefill latency**: `vllm bench latency --batch-size 1 --output-len 1 --num-iters-warmup 5 --num-iters 30 --max-model-len 4096 --seed 0`. One process per run, main and this PR alternating, 3 reps. Each cell is main → this PR, median over reps in ms, with the delta; "~" marks overlapping rep ranges.

| prompt tokens | Qwen3-4B, fp16, sym | Qwen3-8B, fp16, asym | Qwen3-8B, bf16, asym (control) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 64 | 34.9 → 33.0 (−5.4%) | 71.1 → 71.6 (+0.7% ~) | 74.1 → 74.2 (+0.2% ~) |
| 128 | 51.5 → 46.7 (−9.4%) | 92.2 → 92.5 (+0.3% ~) | 96.3 → 96.2 (−0.2% ~) |
| 192 | 76.5 → 72.6 (−5.1%) | 140.9 → 140.3 (−0.4% ~) | 147.9 → 148.0 (+0.0% ~) |
| 256 | 91.1 → 76.5 (−16.0%) | 165.0 → 163.1 (−1.1%) | 174.8 → 172.8 (−1.1% ~) |
| 512 | 175.7 → 144.3 (−17.9%) | 325.7 → 264.5 (−18.8%) | 340.6 → 342.1 (+0.4% ~) |
| 2048 | 782.7 → 673.5 (−14.0%) | 1346.3 → 1118.8 (−16.9%) | 1366.0 → 1364.8 (−0.1% ~) |

**Large batches**: `vllm bench latency --batch-size {128,256} --output-len {1,128} --num-iters-warmup 1 --num-iters 1 --max-model-len 4096 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --max-num-seqs 256 --seed 0`. One process per run, main (11a8d571d2, this PR's parent) and this PR alternating, 3 reps. Each cell is the change in end-to-end latency from main, median over reps; "~" marks overlapping rep ranges.

| batch | prompt tokens | Qwen3-4B fp16 sym, output 1 | Qwen3-4B fp16 sym, output 128 | Qwen3-8B fp16 asym, output 1 | Qwen3-8B fp16 asym, output 128 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 128 | 128 | −47.8% | −26.3% | −51.8% | −28.6% |
| 128 | 256 | −47.2% | −30.9% | −51.9% | −34.8% |
| 128 | 512 | −47.6% | −34.6% | −51.4% | −40.3% |
| 128 | 1024 | −46.9% | −36.1% | −51.1% | −43.0% |
| 256 | 128 | −48.0% | −29.2% | −51.8% | −29.7% |

| 256 | 512 | −47.8% | −35.6% | −51.6% | −41.0% |

Qwen3-8B bf16 (control, prompt 512): batch 128 +2.9% ~ at output 1 and −0.1% ~ at output 128; batch 256 −0.5% ~ and +0.4% ~.

Models are `RedHatAI/Qwen3-4B-quantized.w4a16` and `RedHatAI/Qwen3-8B-quantized.w4a16`.

**Accuracy**: GSM8K, 5-shot, 500 questions, greedy, `tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py` against a server started with `--dtype float16 --max-model-len 4096`. Differences are ±1 question.

| model | dtype | quant | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `RedHatAI/Qwen3-8B-quantized.w4a16` | fp16 | asym | 0.884 | 0.882 |
| `RedHatAI/Qwen3-4B-quantized.w4a16` | fp16 | sym | 0.848 | 0.850 |

**Tests**: 135 passed on gfx1151. CI has no gfx11 runners: the AMD kernel quantization shards run on MI300/MI355, where these tests skip.

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_rdna_hybrid_w4a16.py \
       tests/kernels/quantization/test_w4a16_kernel_selection.py
```

<details>
<summary>Kernel sweep</summary>

Calls `_rdna_hybrid_w4a16_apply_impl` directly with the main and PR copies of `rdna_hybrid_w4a16.py`, timed with `triton.testing.do_bench` and a cache flush between reps, as in `benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_rdna_hybrid_w4a16_gemm.py`. Qwen3-8B and Qwen3-1.7B qkv/o/gate_up/down shapes, group size 32/64/128, M 6–2048, 1248 configs, 3 reps with rotating order. Geomean kernel time vs main; lower is better.

| dtype | quant | M | Qwen3-8B | Qwen3-1.7B |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| fp16 | sym | ≤ 128 | 0.972 | 0.979 |
| fp16 | sym | 129–256 | 0.845 | 0.968 |
| fp16 | sym | > 256 | 0.762 | 0.787 |
| fp16 | asym | ≤ 128 | 0.999 | 0.999 |
| fp16 | asym | 129–256 | 0.996 | 0.999 |
| fp16 | asym | > 256 | 0.766 | 0.795 |
| bf16 | sym | all | 0.997–1.000 | 0.999–1.000 |
| bf16 | asym | all | 0.997–1.000 | 1.000 |

Output bit-identical to main: 1248 of 1248 configs.

Geomeans hide some per-shape losses for symmetric fp16: 46 of its 312 configs are more than 2% slower than main (195 are more than 2% faster). The worst is Qwen3-1.7B `down_proj` (K = 6144, N = 2048) at M = 129–192, 13–22% slower. Every loss was already present in #55711.

</details>

## Details

**Packed dequant.** For a 4-bit value `n`, the bits `0x6400 | n` read as fp16 are exactly `1024 + n`. One `v_and_or_b32` (`(x & 0x000F000F) | 0x64006400`) does this for two values at once, instead of the `v_and_b16` + `v_or_b16` per value that Triton emits. The ExLlama shuffle layout already puts paired values 16 bits apart, so no extra shuffling is needed. The kernel subtracts `1024 + zp` instead of `zp`, which is exact because fp16 represents every integer below 2048.

**When it is used.** Only fp16 on gfx1151, the only GPU it was measured on, decided on the host and passed to the kernel as the `PACKED_DEQUANT` constexpr. Asymmetric layers use it only above M = 256: the extra zero-point load made it 1.2–2.4x slower per GEMM below that.

**Tiles.** The packed fp16 path and the scalar bf16 path want different tiles, most visibly `BLOCK_N` 256 vs 64 at deep M. `_select_skinny_gfx1151_config` picks new tiles and `num_stages=1` for fp16 above M = 128 (M = 256 for asymmetric). Everything else keeps the existing ladder and overrides unchanged. `num_stages=1` stays off bf16, where it cost 15.8% end-to-end on an asymmetric model.

**Numerics.** The dequant result is unchanged. The new tiles change `BLOCK_K`, and with it the fp32 accumulation order, so fp16 output is not guaranteed bit-identical. In the kernel sweep it was bit-identical in all 1248 configs.

**Not duplicating.** #57199 changes the HIP decode kernel, not the Triton prefill path. #52637 changes symmetric weight loading in `process_weights_after_loading`. #60710 adds an opt-in (default off) dense weight cache that skips the int4 dequant at M ≥ 256; it edits the same file but leaves the Triton dequant and tile selection alone. No other open PR touches the prefill dequant or the gfx1151 tile selection.

## Details

**Packed dequant.** For a 4-bit value `n`, the bits `0x6400 | n` read as fp16 are exactly `1024 + n`. One `v_and_or_b32` (`(x & 0x000F000F) | 0x64006400`) does this for two values at once, instead of the `v_and_b16` + `v_or_b16` per value that Triton emits. The ExLlama shuffle layout already puts paired values 16 bits apart, so no extra shuffling is needed. The kernel subtracts `1024 + zp` instead of `zp`, which is exact because fp16 represents every integer below 2048.

**When it is used.** Only fp16 on gfx1151, the only GPU it was measured on, decided on the host and passed to the kernel as the `PACKED_DEQUANT` constexpr. Asymmetric layers use it only above M = 256: the extra zero-point load made it 1.2–2.4x slower per GEMM below that.

**Numerics.** The dequant result is unchanged. The new tiles change `BLOCK_K`, and with it the fp32 accumulation order, so fp16 output is not guaranteed bit-identical. In the kernel sweep it was bit-identical in all 1248 configs.
